name: NC_001604.1
novelty: Has a relative in the training set (PV223880.1, Escherichia, similarity 0.90). Honest validation applies at the default level (macro-F1 ~0.63).
notes: Top two candidates are both Enterobacteriaceae (Escherichia/Klebsiella/Salmonella). This is the model's known weak spot; treat the host as 'Enterobacteriaceae, genus unresolved' until tested.
steps: Search for a known relative: BLASTn against NCBI Virus / INPHARED. If a close hit has a recorded host, that evidence outranks this model.
Annotate the genome (e.g. Pharokka, which uses PHANOTATE; tRNAscan-SE for tRNAs) and check completeness (CheckV).

Predict lifestyle (e.g. BACPHLIP) and screen for integrase/repressor genes, toxins, virulence and antibiotic-resistance genes (e.g. ABRicate with VFDB/CARD, or AMRFinderPlus). Temperate phages or phages carrying such genes are generally unsuitable for therapy.
Place it taxonomically (e.g. VIRIDIC, vConTACT) to see which known phage group it belongs to. Strain-level identity needs reference-based comparison; this model does not give it.
Confirm the host in the lab: spot assay / efficiency of plating on a panel of Escherichia strains.

Only if the goal is to express or clone a gene or region (e.g. an endolysin or a receptor-binding protein): pick it from the annotation, compare its codon usage/GC with the expression host (this genome is 48.4% GC), design primers, and choose a vector accordingly. Cloning a whole phage genome into a plasmid is not routine; genome engineering uses different workflows (e.g. yeast-based or cell-free rebooting).
